INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE JULY 6, 2020
  OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUISNESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT MEETING

The Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District meeting will be closed to the public in
compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-
19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting will be conducted via teleconference with members
participating remotely. Considering this, the customary meeting format has been modified.
Even with this change in format, the City is still encouraging public participation and wishes to
make residents aware of the following opportunities for participation:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

  2) Send an email in advance if you wish to make a comment on a specific agenda item.
  Please submit your comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. We ask that
  you provide those emails before 7:00 a.m. on July 6th so that staff will be prepared to
  read them aloud at the appropriate time during the meeting.

  3) If you wish to make a comment during the meeting, we will be monitoring the above
  email address and will make every effort to include your comment into the records.
  Please be aware there is a delay in the live stream service and any comments should
  be submitted as soon as possible.

  4) For individuals that wish to share their comments directly during the live stream, you
  may email the planning@cityoflaverne.org by 7:00 a.m. on July 6th with a phone
  number and the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate
  time during the meeting for your comment.

  A.  Discussion on Upcoming Events (cool cruise, Beer/wine walk, etc.)  -
  Mr. Walters statid in order to move forward with Cool Cruise we need to receive
  provisional approval at the next City Council meeting.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the final decision to continue with the event must be made
  by August 3,2020.

  Mr. Walters stated that Beer & Wine Walk discussion would be held until next
  meeting on Monday, August 3'd.

  It was moved by Mr. Gendreau and seconded by Ms. Stark to ask City Council for
  provisional approval for the Cool Cruise event. Motion carried by 5-0 vote.

  B.  D Street Closure for Restaurants - Mr. Scherer stated that due to the Governor's
  order restaurants are now closed for indoor dining. It was decided by the City to
  close D Street between Bonita Avenue and Third Street to expand outdoor dining'
  picnic tables were placed throughout D Street and in Transportation Plaza. Staff
  was later assigned io sanitize the tables after each use. Restaurants like Roberta's
  Village Inn and Lordsburg Taphouse extended their own seating into the sidewalk
  and street. ABC approval is required to serve alcohol and a no fee City permit is
  required for expanded outdoor dining.

  Ms. Stark asked if there was any concern from the health department with placing
  picnic tables on the dirt area of Transportation Plaza.

  Mr. Scherer stated that these tables were set up for take-out orders only.
   Ms. Rehm stated that she was only open Thursday and Friday due to the holiday
  and was not sure of the effect on her business. She stated that all her customers
  provided positive feedback.

  Mr. Scherer read public comments received by Roberta Virgin of Roberta's
  Village Inn and Amanda Clarke from Roots Salon both in support of the street
  closure. Mr. Scherer stated other messages were received but not officially
  through the email plannine@cityoflaverne.org.

  Mr. Walters stated that he was impressed with the tree lights and the number of
  people on the streets.

  Mr. Walters suggested banners promoting outdoor seating and Ms. Stark
  suggested signage for parking at Lot E.

  Ms. Rehm asked if the City would provide water stations'

  Mr. Scherer stated that if the closure goes beyond one week the City would be
  more likely to provide water stations.
